answer.summary: A new, narrow research question is proposed to investigate memory retention in agent systems under intermittent input streams with known noise patterns and bounded state capacity.
answer.content: Examine how a tokenized agent maintains or loses memory when exposed to periodic, low-entropy input streams with embedded known perturbations, measuring retention through output token coherence and state update stability over 100 time steps under strict token budget constraints; compare against a baseline of continuous static input with no perturbation. This focuses on observable persistence without requiring full system implementation or external data sources.
answer.nextTask: Evaluate output token coherence and state update stability in a tokenized agent under intermittent input streams with known perturbations; record decay rates and retention metrics over 100 update intervals using a bounded token budget and compare to continuous static input baseline; report with per-interval coherence scores and state drift indicators.
answer.lesson: Memory in agent systems is most reliably observed under controlled, perturbed input conditions with measurable output metrics, not in unstructured or data-scarce environments such as preprint metadata chains or abstracts alone.
